Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Power Generation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Lisa Chen, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Power Generation's Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; and David Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mark Thompson.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Lisa, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong operational performance in our generation fleet, continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio, effective cost management, and progress on our infrastructure investments.

As we wrap up our Q3 results, I want to update you on the progress we're making against these strategic initiatives and our long-term goals. At Apex Power Generation, our guiding principle is to deliver reliable, affordable, and increasingly clean power to our 12 million customers across our 15-state footprint, while setting the company up for sustainable growth amid the shifting energy landscape. We're intensely focused on three core pillars: speeding up the clean energy transition, upgrading our grid for greater resilience and to handle electrification, and pursuing operational excellence to meet surging demand from data centers, electric vehicles, and industrial reshoring.

On the clean energy transition front, which anchors our net-zero by 2045 target—five years ahead of competitors like Duke Energy or Southern Company—we commissioned 450 MW of fresh renewables in Q3, such as the 250 MW Solar Ridge initiative in Texas' ERCOT market and 200 MW from our initial utility-scale offshore wind project off Virginia, partnered with Ørsted. Year-to-date, that's 1.2 GW of renewable additions, surpassing our full-year goal of 1 GW by 15%. Our renewable capacity has reached 18 GW, making up 42% of our overall 43 GW portfolio, improved from 35% only 18 months back. Our development pipeline surpasses 25 GW, including 8 GW under construction or in late-stage permitting, notably 4 GW of solar-plus-storage hybrids in PJM and MISO territories.

We've advanced significantly on phasing out older assets too. Consistent with our decarbonization plan, we idled 800 MW of our most dated coal units at the Midwestern Basin facility in Q3, cutting Scope 1 emissions 12% year-over-year. This was balanced by adding 600 MW of new natural gas peakers with GE Vernova's HA-class turbines to maintain reliability through last summer's extreme heat. Importantly, we're pushing forward with carbon capture for our leftover 2.5 GW coal assets; Phase 1 at Riverbend Station employs Mitsubishi Heavy Industries' cutting-edge solvent technology, capturing 90% of CO2 at pilot levels, aiming for full rollout by 2026. These steps keep us on pace for a 55% emissions drop by 2030 from our 2005 baseline, aided by $450 million in IRA tax credits booked so far this year.

Shifting to grid modernization, we're committing substantial resources to accommodate booming load growth—projected at a 2.5% CAGR through 2030, propelled by hyperscale data centers from partners like Microsoft and Google. Our $2.8 billion capex plan this year allocates $1.1 billion to transmission and distribution enhancements. A key achievement is our 300 MWh battery energy storage system rollout in California's CAISO, linked to Fluence's Gridstack platform, which supplied 150 MW of ancillary services during peak periods, yielding $25 million in revenue at 15% IRR. We've also implemented advanced metering infrastructure for 2.5 million customers, supporting dynamic pricing that reduced system peak demand by 8% in fast-growing Southeast areas like Florida and Georgia.

Across regions, results are robust. In ERCOT, renewables form 55% of our mix, and we've locked in 1.2 GW of new PPAs with tech companies at 20% premiums over market rates, backing our 12-14% regulated ROE. PJM values our flexible resources, with gas fleet availability at 95% during events similar to Winter Storm Elliott. In the Northeast, our New York ISO hydro assets deliver reliable 10% returns, buffering natural gas price swings.

Operationally, these efforts are paying dividends. Renewables and storage adjusted EBITDA reached $350 million in Q3, a 28% YoY rise, with margins climbing to 65% via O&M savings from our AspenTech-powered digital twin platform. Customer satisfaction stays elite at 92% per J.D. Power, boosted by EV programs: 5,000 Level 2 chargers installed and 250,000 customers in demand response, saving $100 million in capex.

Ahead of the pack on electrification, our joint venture with Tesla for 1 GW of Megapack storage tackles wind intermittency in Midwest markets. We're also pursuing small modular reactors with NuScale Power, eyeing 300 MW by 2029 to support baseload as data center loads could add 15 GW to our territory by 2030's end.

To sum up, we're nailing execution on long-term objectives: 60% renewables by 2030, $5-6 billion annual capex at 10-12% returns, and 7-9% EPS compounding. These moves de-risk us against regs like FERC Order 2020 and tap the $1 trillion U.S. clean energy market. Now, I'll hand over to CFO Sarah Reynolds for details on the quarter.

Sarah Reynolds: Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone, and thanks for being on our Q3 earnings call for Apex Power Generation. Before diving into the financials, let me update you on our advancements toward clean energy targets and emission cuts—a key element of our enduring strategy that curbs regulatory and climate exposures while fueling growth in the energy shift. We've pledged a 60% drop in Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions from our 2005 base by 2030, net-zero ops by 2040, and net-zero across the value chain by 2050, matching Science Based Targets and the Paris 1.5°C trajectory.

The metrics highlight this. Through Q3 year-to-date, CO2 emissions fell 28% YoY, with trailing 12-month Scope 1 and 2 at 42 million metric tons versus 58 million last year. Emission intensity hit 320 lbs CO2/MWh, 15% better than 2023's 375 lbs/MWh, thanks to coal retirements and renewables expansion. Clean sources now make 42% of our generation mix, from 35% a year ago, beating our 40% 2025 goal. Renewables generated 18.7 TWh in nine months, up 22% YoY, with solar at 26.5% capacity factor and onshore wind at 38.2%, topping EIA averages.

By region, gains vary with our spread. Southeast—serving 12 million in Georgia, Carolinas, Florida—saw 1,800 MW coal retired since 2022, including Brunswick County early, slashing Scope 1 by 35% to hit EPA Clean Air Act and state carbon limits. Texas ERCOT (25% of portfolio) added 850 MW solar-plus-storage in Permian this quarter, IRA-boosted ITC/PTC for $28/MWh LCOE matching gas peakers. Midwest 2.2 GW wind in Illinois/Iowa hit 41% factor for 7.2 TWh YTD, plus 15-year 1 GW PPA with Meta from 2026.

Beyond capacity, we're blending tech for stability. Battery pipeline: 2.4 GW/8 GWh over 12 projects; Arizona's Desert Sun 400 MW/1.6 GWh with Tesla Megapacks and AI EMS at 95% efficiency, yielding $45 million ancillary revenue to PJM/MISO, up 60% YoY. Innovation includes Wyoming DAC pilot with Occidental at Natrium nuclear site for 500,000 tons CO2/year by 2027 at ~$250/ton, and GE Vernova H-class gas turbines with 30% H2 blend at three peakers, cutting emissions 12% sans output loss.

These drive regulated/unregulated expansion. Q3 clean capex $1.2 billion, 20% over plan, via 4.8% cost debt and $2.5 billion YTD green bonds at 10-15 bps premium. 5.5 GW new hyperscaler PPAs (AWS, Microsoft) at 12% IRR, 80% debt. RECs added $120 million EBITDA at $15/MWh premium in NY/CA RPS.

Forward, IRA transferability nets $450 million 2024 credits; DOE loans may hasten 3 GW offshore Carolinas. Supply bifacial panels and 2,000 GW queues per FERC are hurdles, but 1.3x DSC and $4.2 billion liquidity cushion us.

Overall, clean momentum builds environmental and shareholder wins. Renewables to 55% mix by 2030, outpacing NextEra/Dominion emissions while 7-9% EPS CAGR.

Now, let me review our Q3 2024 financials versus prior year and quarter, key drivers, and updated outlook. All adjusted, excluding $45 million NUG MTM gain and prior restructuring. See slides 8-14 for recs/segments.

Headlines: Q3 revenues $3.25 billion, +8% YoY from $3.01 billion, +5% sequential from Q2 $3.09 billion. Adjusted EBITDA $1.12 billion, +12% YoY from $1.00 billion, +1% from Q2 $1.11 billion. Adjusted EPS $1.48, topping guide midpoint, +11% YoY from $1.33, +7% from Q2 $1.38. This underscores our diversified portfolio—47% renewables, 32% nat gas CC, 15% nuclear, rest coal/peaters—amid load surge, ERCOT/PJM auctions, cost discipline.

Regulated Utilities (55% EBITDA): Revenues +6% YoY to $1.45 billion on 4.2% Southeast retail load growth (GA, Carolinas, FL) from electrification/hyperscalers. Normalized weather vs last year's +15% CDDs; +2.5% seq from Q2 via rate base from $2.1 billion capex incl 400 MW solar-storage at Brunswick. ROE 10.8% with FERC rates, $180 million AFUDC on offshore wind T&D.

Competitive Generation (ERCOT/MISO/PJM merchant): +22% YoY revenues to $1.05 billion. Gas CF 62% vs 55%, 1.2 GW new GE 7HA.02 at Rio Grande CCCT South TX, 58% HR, 85% gas hedged $3.25/MMBtu collars. Solar +28% YoY 1.8 million MWh, 350 MW First Solar Series 7 PPAs tech. Wind +15% YoY 2.2 million MWh despite La Niña. Storage 1.2 GW/12 sites doubled dispatch rev to $120 million on CAISO/ERCOT volatility.

Thermal: Revenues -5% YoY to $650 million on 800 MW coal idle for MISO 2025 decarbon. Nuclear steady 92% CF, 2.4 million MWh (Palo Verde/Vogtle-like). Fuel $28/MWh blended, -3% vs guide, 75% hedged coal, gas swaps to 2026.

O&M +4% YoY to $620 million, below $650 million guide via Oracle APM, drone wind maint. Q3 capex $850 million, FY track $3.3 billion, 40% renewables/grid post-Idalia.

YTD EBITDA $3.35 billion +10% 2023, EPS $4.25 vs $3.92. Trends: 7% load growth (2x US avg), AI data centers 15% TX incr demand, EVs. IRA PTC $27/MWh legacy wind, 30% storage ITC: $450 million tax equity like NextEra/Orsted.

Guidance: FY24 adj EPS midpoint raised to $5.95 ($5.90-$6.00 prior $5.80-$6.00), norm weather, gas $3.00-$3.50 NYMEX, no disallowances. EBITDA $4.45-$4.55 billion, +$100 million midpoint on renewables, -$75 million storm avoid. Capex $3.3 billion.

2025 init adj EPS $6.40-$6.70, +9% midpoint: 6% rate base to $45 billion, 1.5 GW renewables/storage (600 MW ERCOT solar BESS PPA), $200 million CCUS nat gas for EPA 111. Risks: turbine delays, PJM ROE; upsides TX grid, DOE T&D loans.

Net-zero 2045 accel: 10 GW renewables queue, 3 GW storage 2027, NuScale SMR 300 MW 2029 MOUs. Like Dominion hybrid + merchant upside.

Our capex for the quarter was $850 million, primarily focused on renewables and thermal sustainment. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders.

Mark Thompson: Thank you, Sarah. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. We'll now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Julien Dumoulin-Smith with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Julien Dumoulin-Smith, BofA: Thanks, good morning everyone. Strong quarter here—beat on adjusted EBITDA by about 8% or so. Can you walk us through the key drivers behind the upside, particularly on the generation side? And how much of that was weather versus dispatch? Also, any color on the forward capacity auction results in PJM for your fleet?

Sarah Reynolds: Good morning, Julien. Appreciate the question. Yes, we delivered adjusted EBITDA of $1.12 billion for Q3, up 12% year-over-year and around $95 million above the midpoint of our guidance. On generation, thermal assets led with about 60% of the beat. CCGTs in PJM and MISO hit fleet-wide 68% capacity factor from 62% last year, fueled by high spark spreads at $45/MMBtu average in Mid-Atlantic hubs. Weather contributed—PJM had 15% hotter-than-normal HDDs—but dispatch drove it; we optimized 4.2 GW gas for 250 GWh extra output at over $120/MWh realized.

Nuclear stable at 93% across 2.8 GW, no refuel slips. Renewables gave $25 million boost from wind—1.5 GW onshore at 38% vs 35% long-term target—plus IRA PTC inflation tweaks.

PJM capacity: Cleared 100% of 3.1 GW eligible at $269/MW-day average for 2025/26 BRA, +40% prior. Locks $450 million revenue; peakers scored under RPM. No must-runs, merchant at 40% portfolio.

Operator: Next question from David Arcaro with Morgan Stanley.

David Arcaro, MS: Thanks. Sarah, great color. Shifting to capex—your FY24 guide came in at $2.8-3.0 billion, skewed to the high end now. Breakdown on renewables versus thermal sustainment? And strategically, with data center RFPs flooding in from hyperscalers like Google and Microsoft, how are you positioning the portfolio? Any updates on battery co-locates or green hydrogen pilots?

Mark Thompson: David, thanks. Capex ramping per plan—Q3 $780 million, FY track $2.95 billion. Renewables 55% or $1.6 billion: Pushing 800 MW solar+storage ERCOT (Black Rock, Horizon), 450 MW ITC-qualifying IRA $120 million credits. Hybrids—350 MW/1.4 GWh BESS 4-hr—for arbitrage, intermittency hedge like CAISO. Wind 200 MW Plains, 42% factor via tall hubs/repowers.

Thermal sustainment $900 million: $400 million CCGT overhauls <7,000 BTU/kWh HR, $250 million nuclear uprates Salem to 2053 +50 MW MUR. Rest transmission incl $200 million FERC 1920.

Data centers: Demand booming—PJM load +15% CAGR 2030 from AI hyperscalers vs 4% base. Signed 1.2 GW PPAs Meta/AWS $85-95/MWh fixed 15-yr, 20% CPI escalators. Positioning: Co-loc 500 MW solar+BESS with 300 MW VA data campus—zero-carbon RECs, future CCUS. Cumberland gas H2 pilot: 10 MW electrolyzer curtailed wind, 20% H2 duct burners by 2026, 11-12% ROE hurdle.

Operator: Our next question is from Neil Hanson with Oppenheimer.

Neil Hanson, Oppenheimer: Morning, team. Regulatory backdrop—nice wins on FERC transmission ROE adders, but state-level risks in California and New York with rooftop solar pushback. How does that flow to earnings? And on coal retirements, your 1.2 GW fleet—any divestiture updates amid activist pressure?

Sarah Reynolds: Neil, spot on. FERC 10.6% base ROE +50-100 bps recon adders = $150 million EPS over 5 years—$1.2 billion T&D queue full benefit. CPUC NEM 3.0 headwind: CA utilities 8% export compression, -$40 million Q3 DG margins, offset 12% rate base wildfire capex. NY CLCPA: Litigation risk low—2 GW upstate hydro/solar gets ZEC $80/MWh to 2028.

Coal: Optimizing. Cumberland 600 MW retired MATS, NuScale SMR study $2 billion 10% IRR post-45Q. Remaining 600 MW 85% hedged 2026 $35/MMBtu NYMEX; sales to data off-takers baseload. Activist talks good—ESG A- Sustainalytics on 45% carbon cut since 2020.

Operator: Question from Angie Storozynski with Seaport Global.

Angie Storozynski, Seaport: Hi all. Fuel hedging—your gas book looks tight at 90% for 2025. Thoughts on winter volatility post-Ukraine? And merchant exposure: ERCOT upside from heat domes, but any curtailment risk with 15 GW renewables in queue?

Mark Thompson: Angie, hedging solid. Gas: 92% winter 24/25 $3.85/MMBtu blended Appalachian, 75% summer $4.20. Ukraine/LNG supportive—EIA $3.50 Henry Hub '25 avg, hedges PJM winters vs '22/'23 vortex. Coal 100%; U $65/lb U3O8 long-term.

ERCOT merchant 35% accretive—Q3 $110/MWh 1.8 GW gas/wind in 105°F dome (lambda $9k/MWh). Curtailment: 2.5 GW batteries (+500 MW YTD) catch 95% ORDC, AI scarcity opt. PUCT queue ok—1 GW solar+storage COD 2027. +$200 million '25 EBITDA heat models.

Operator: Final question from Nick Lawson with Deutsche Bank.

Nick Lawson, DB: Thanks. Long-term EPS guide—$4.80-5.20 for FY25, implying 7% growth. Sensitivities to load growth, rates, and IRA? And M&A pipeline post your Entergy joint venture on offshore wind?

Sarah Reynolds: Nick, FY25 base EPS midpoint $5.00, +8% '24. Load +6% YoY (data 40%); rates 5.25% 10Y. Sens: +1% load +$0.15 EPS; -50 bps rates -$0.20; IRA ITC/PTC +$0.25 (700 MW). Entergy offshore JV: Garden State II 500 MW NJ monopiles 50% own—PPA $110/MWh, FID Q4'24, 12% IRR IIJA.

M&A: Southeast nuclear bolt-ons <$1 billion, Midwest storage. Reg ROE 10.5% prefs; 1-2% EPS acc, no megadeals. Questions?

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. That concludes today's Q&A. Thank you for joining Apex Power Generation's Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Management will be available for follow-ups. This call is now adjourned.

Mark Thompson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Apex Power Generation for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Apex Power Generation.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
